lines.text: 3.5 How Do We Test for Nutrients?
So far you have taken this chapter's word for it. Time to check for yourself.
Some nutrients need a well-equipped laboratory to detect. Three do not: starch,
fat and protein can each be tested with equipment a school already has. Starch,
incidentally, is a carbohydrate — the form in which plants store it.
Before you begin, one habit worth building. Before each test, write down what
you expect to happen. That written expectation is a prediction, and it is not a
guess — it is your current understanding, put on record where the result can
